questions.question: A laptop is priced at ₹40,000. A customer gets a discount of ₹4,000 on it. After the discount, the customer buys a mouse whose marked price is ₹1,500 at a discount of 20%. What is the total amount the customer spends on both items?
questions.questionHtml: A laptop is priced at ₹40,000. A customer gets a discount of ₹4,000 on it. After the discount, the customer buys a mouse whose marked price is ₹1,500 at a discount of 20%. What is the total amount the customer spends on both items?
questions.solution:
⇒ Laptop selling price = 40000 − 4000 = 36000

⇒ Discount on mouse = 1500 × 20 ÷ 100 = 300

⇒ Mouse selling price = 1500 − 300 = 1200

⇒ Total amount spent = 36000 + 1200 = 37200

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 18 and 24 minutes respectively. After both are opened together for 6 minutes, the rate of pipe A becomes half, and pipe B becomes double its original. In how many more minutes will the tank be full?
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 18 and 24 minutes respectively. After both are opened together for 6 minutes, the rate of pipe A becomes half, and pipe B becomes double its original. In how many more minutes will the tank be full?
questions.solution:
⇒ LCM of 18 and 24 = 72 units

⇒ Efficiency of A = 72 ÷ 18 = 4 units/min, Efficiency of B = 72 ÷ 24 = 3 units/min

⇒ Combined efficiency = 4 + 3 = 7 units/min, Work done in 6 min = 7 × 6 = 42 units

⇒ Remaining work = 72 − 42 = 30 units

⇒ New efficiency of A = 4 ÷ 2 = 2 units/min, New efficiency of B = 3 × 2 = 6 units/min

⇒ New combined efficiency = 2 + 6 = 8 units/min, Time required = 30 ÷ 8 = 3.75 min

options.html: B2 = AC

  <!-- ZONE 1: MECHANISM FIGURE -->

  <circle cx="70" cy="65" r="32" fill="#ddeeff" stroke="#2255cc" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="70" y="70" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#2255cc">A</text>
  <text x="70" y="25" font-family="Arial" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2255cc">Principal (P1)</text>
  
  <!-- Transformation Arrow 1 -->
  <path d="M105,65 Q155,25 205,65" fill="none" stroke="#555555" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="2,1" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <text x="155" y="35" font-family="Arial" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="#555555">SI = B</text>

  <!-- Coin B (Interest of A / Principal for C) -->
  <circle cx="240" cy="65" r="32" fill="#ede7f6" stroke="#6a1b9a" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="240" y="70" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#6a1b9a">B</text>
  <text x="240" y="110" font-family="Arial" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6a1b9a">Interest (I1) / Principal (P2)</text>

  <!-- Transformation Arrow 2 -->
  <path d="M275,65 Q325,25 375,65" fill="none" stroke="#555555" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="2,1" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <text x="325" y="35" font-family="Arial" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="#555555">SI = C</text>

  <!-- Coin C (Final Interest) -->
  <circle cx="410" cy="65" r="32" fill="#fff0cc" stroke="#cc5500" stroke-width="2"/>

  <text x="155" y="85" font-family="Arial" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="#555555">Rate = R%, Time = T</text>
  <text x="325" y="85" font-family="Arial" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="#555555">Rate = R%, Time = T</text>

  <text x="30" y="140" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#222222">⇒ B = (A × R × T) ÷ 100 → (RT ÷ 100) = B ÷ A</text>

questions.question: A hemisphere of radius 5 cm is carved from a sphere. What is the volume of the hemisphere?
questions.questionHtml: A hemisphere of radius 5 cm is carved from a sphere. What is the volume of the hemisphere?
questions.solution:
Let r = 5 cm

Volume of hemisphere = (2 × π × r3) ÷ 3

⇒ Volume = (2 × π × 53) ÷ 3 = (2 × π × 125) ÷ 3 = 250π ÷ 3 cm3

questions.question: A solid sphere is placed inside a cube such that it touches all six faces. What percentage of the cube's volume is not occupied by the sphere?
questions.questionHtml: A solid sphere is placed inside a cube such that it touches all six faces. What percentage of the cube's volume is not occupied by the sphere?
questions.solution:
Let side of cube = 2r, radius of sphere = r.

Volume of cube = (2r)3 = 8r3.

Volume of sphere = (4 × π × r3) ÷ 3.

Unoccupied volume = 8r3 − (4 × π × r3) ÷ 3 = r3(8 − 4π ÷ 3).

Percentage not occupied = ((8 − 4π ÷ 3) ÷ 8) × 100 = (1 − π ÷ 6) × 100 ≈ 47.67%.

questions.question: The sides of a rectangular prism are in the ratio 4:5:6. If the volume of the prism is 960 cm³ what is the length of its longest side?
questions.questionHtml: The sides of a rectangular prism are in the ratio 4:5:6. If the volume of the prism is 960 cm³ what is the length of its longest side?
questions.solution:
Let sides be 4x, 5x, 6x.

Volume = 4x × 5x × 6x = 120x3.

120x3 = 960 ⇒ x3 = 960 ÷ 120 ⇒ x = 2.

Longest side = 6x = 6 × 2 = 12 cm.

questions.question: A conical bucket is cut at one-third its height from the top. What is the ratio of the volumes of the two parts (top part to bottom part)?
questions.questionHtml: A conical bucket is cut at one-third its height from the top. What is the ratio of the volumes of the two parts (top part to bottom part)?
questions.solution:
Volume of cone = (1 ÷ 3) × π × r2 × h

Height of top small cone = h ÷ 3

Ratio of heights (small : original) = 1 : 3

Ratio of volumes (small : original) = 13 : 33

Ratio of volumes (small : original) = 1 : 27

Volume of bottom part = 27 − 1 = 26 parts

Required ratio (top : bottom) = 1 : 26

questions.question: If tanA + cotA = 2 and A ∈ (0, π/2), then what is sinA + cosA?
questions.questionHtml: If tanA + cotA = 2 and A ∈ (0, π/2), then what is sinA + cosA?
questions.solution:
⇒ tanA + cotA = sinA ÷ cosA + cosA ÷ sinA

⇒ tanA + cotA = (sin2A + cos2A) ÷ (sinA × cosA)

⇒ 1 ÷ (sinA × cosA) = 2

⇒ sinA × cosA = 1 ÷ 2

⇒ 2sinA cosA = 1

⇒ sin2A = 1

⇒ 2A = π ÷ 2

⇒ A = π ÷ 4

⇒ sinA = 1 ÷ √2, cosA = 1 ÷ √2

⇒ sinA + cosA = 1 ÷ √2 + 1 ÷ √2

⇒ sinA + cosA = 2 ÷ √2

questions.question: A right-angled triangle has a hypotenuse of 13 cm and one leg of 5 cm. A second right-angled triangle is similar to the first, and its hypotenuse is 39 cm. What is the area of the second triangle?
questions.questionHtml: A right-angled triangle has a hypotenuse of 13 cm and one leg of 5 cm. A second right-angled triangle is similar to the first, and its hypotenuse is 39 cm. What is the area of the second triangle?
questions.solution:
⇒ Perpendicular2 = 132 − 52

⇒ Perpendicular2 = 169 − 25 = 144

⇒ Perpendicular = 12 cm

⇒ Area of first triangle = (1 ÷ 2) × 5 × 12 = 30 cm2

⇒ Scale factor = 39 ÷ 13 = 3

⇒ Ratio of areas = 32 = 9

⇒ Area of second triangle = 30 × 9 = 270 cm2

questions.question: In a quadrilateral ABCD, a line segment BD is a diagonal such that AB=CD and ∠ABD=∠CDB. Are the triangles ABD and CDB congruent? If so, by what rule?
questions.questionHtml: In a quadrilateral ABCD, a line segment BD is a diagonal such that AB=CD and ∠ABD=∠CDB. Are the triangles ABD and CDB congruent? If so, by what rule?
questions.solution:
AB = CD

BD = BD

∠ABD = ∠CDB

⇒ Two sides and the included angle are equal

⇒ ΔABD ≅ ΔCDB by SAS rule

questions.question: The length of each of two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle is 10 cm. What is the approximate distance from the external point to the center of the circle, if the radius is 6 cm?
questions.questionHtml: The length of each of two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle is 10 cm. What is the approximate distance from the external point to the center of the circle, if the radius is 6 cm?
questions.solution:
Distance = √(Tangent Length2 + Radius2)

⇒ Distance = √(102 + 62)

⇒ Distance = √(100 + 36) = √136 ≈ 11.66 cm ≈ 12 cm
